paras: The Oakwood handcar ambush took place about October 5, 1903, when a citizen posse at Oakwood, Illinois, derailed a handcar carrying three Black men accused of burglary and fired on them. The three men escaped after a running fight, and one member of the posse was grazed by a bullet. Danville dispatches reported it as a battle with "negro burglars."

According to a Danville special dated October 5, returning excursionists surprised three men early that morning in William Lynch's store at Muncie, eight miles east of Danville. The men took a Big Four handcar and pumped west toward Oakwood, whose citizens were warned by telephone. Village Clerk Robert S. Pinager organized a posse, twelve men according to the Rock Island Argus, which laid a plank secured by a crowbar across the track and hid in the bushes.

The handcar struck the obstruction at top speed and went about four feet into the air. The St. Louis Republic said the men were not hurt and began running as the posse opened fire, while the Argus said they were "pitched headlong to the ground." A running fight through the village followed, with many shots exchanged, until the men outran their pursuers and disappeared in the darkness. One posse member's arm was grazed by a bullet; the special added that one or more of the men were believed struck by small shot.
The Argus reported that officers had failed to trace the men, and no report of an arrest or identification appears in the coverage.

The Indianapolis Journal and the St. Louis Republic printed nearly identical specials on October 6, the Republic under "Fought Running Battle With Negro Burglars." The Argus ran a rewrite on October 7 headlined "Negro Burglars Get Worst of It," although its own text said the men got away. All three told the story from the posse's side and identified the men only by race and the accusation. No Black-press coverage of the episode was found.
The Argus dated its dispatch October 7, but the October 5 specials appeared in print a day earlier.

reader.title: Oakwood handcar ambush
bases: A posse of Oakwood citizens derailed a handcar carrying three Black men accused of burglary and fired on them in a running fight; no one was reported killed (A1, A2, A3).
All three reports are versions of one Danville dispatch: A1 and A2 share nearly the same wording and A3 is a rewrite; no independent local or Black-press account was found.

accounts.label: Danville special (Republic / Indianapolis Journal)
accounts.gist: Excursionists surprised three Black burglars at Muncie; an Oakwood posse threw their handcar with a plank, the men were not hurt and ran under fire, and they escaped; one posseman was grazed and one or more burglars were believed hit by small shot.

accounts.label: Danville wire rewrite (Rock Island Argus)
accounts.gist: A posse of twelve under the town clerk wrecked the handcar, the men were 'pitched headlong', and a running fight through the village followed; one posse member was grazed and officers had not traced the robbers.

framing.detail: Straight news specials under headlines such as 'Fought Running Battle With Negro Burglars' and 'Escaped on Handcar', telling the story from the posse's side.
The Argus headlined it 'Negro Burglars Get Worst of It' with the subhead 'Citizens ... Find and Route Housebreakers', though its own text says the men escaped.

versions.value: Early morning of Oct. 5 (dispatch dated Oct. 5, 'early this morning')

conflicts.note: The Oct. 5 specials appeared in print on Oct. 6, before the Oct. 7 dateline; A3 is a later rewrite, so about Oct. 5 is the better-supported date.
Spelling variant of the same official; the original specials' form may be the more direct.
